title: positioning-canvas template variables
description: Values for templates/positioning-canvas.md.j2 and templates/positioning-canvas.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from positioning-canvas.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

alternatives.title: Alternatives
alternatives.description: What do these customers do instead today? Include doing nothing and the spreadsheet - the alternatives you lose to most are rarely the vendors you benchmark against.

best_fit_customer.title: Best fit customer
best_fit_customer.description: Who is the best-fit customer, in the words they would use about themselves? Specific enough that a reader can name a company that is NOT one - section 4 is where you got this.

market_category.title: Market category
market_category.description: Which category do you want the buyer to file you under? The frame that makes your unique attributes look obvious; the wrong category makes them look irrelevant.

product_name.description: Which product is being positioned - the name a customer would recognise? Positioning one product at a time is the whole method; a portfolio canvas positions nothing.

trigger_event.title: Trigger event
trigger_event.description: What happens in that customer's world that starts the search? An event with a date, not a state of mind - 'closed a Series A', not 'cares about quality'.

unique_value.title: Unique value
unique_value.description: What value do you deliver that the alternatives cannot truthfully claim? Quantified, and traceable to an attribute in section 2 rather than to an adjective.
